correctness.rationale: PASS: Sense-preserving J_f>0 makes h′ nonvanishing and analytic ω with |ω|<1; all formulae on fixed r<1 avoid global disk boundary integrability. Let u=-log(1-|ω|²); direct Wirtinger gives u_z=barω ω′/(1-|ω|²) and Δu=4|ω′|²/(1-|ω|²)². For H=h″/h′ holomorphic the e^{iθ} first angular moment vanishes. Polar derivative e^{iθ}u_z=(u_r−i u_θ/r)/2 averages to U′(r)/2. Therefore average e^{iθ}A_f=−r−(1−r²)U′(r)/4; Green/divergence formula 2πr U′=4∫_{|z|<r} hyperbolic density yields claimed exact negative real first Fourier moment and lower bound by maximum. For ω=az, h=z, g=az²/2 with |a|<1, A_f=−bar z[1+|a|²(1−r²)/(2(1−|a|²r²))] has constant Fourier phase and integral π|a|²r²/(1−|a|²r²), showing sharpness for each r including constant ω boundary. For criterion (3), Schwarz–Pick |ω*|≤1 and division where ω′≠0 gives |A_f|≤1/4; r=1/2 bound contradicts nonconstant ω. For constant ω, S_h=0 means holomorphic Möbius; converse immediate. Finite model examples are illustrative, not infinite proof.
